subject: asp-es
title: ASP.ES.------AF.DY.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-22, where Braxton argues that 'the significance of a given spectacle diversion lies in its ability to progressionally re-dictate the reality dynamics of its time zone — or focus.' (C)ASP-ES (aspect essence) is crossed with AF-DY (affinity dynamics): the question is what aspect-essence compression does to affinity dynamics across the culture. The main line runs from (c)asp-es to AF-DY (the crossing partner). INFO-DE (information degrees) branches from the main line and carries LK-IMP (linkage implications). From AF-DY a line drops to IST-S-ALGN (isolated systematic alignment); from that line a long line runs to LANG-DY (language dynamics), which carries MTA-IMP (meta-implications), with (R)INT (the reality of intention) hanging from it, and MT-TFS-AT (multi-transfer shift activity), which leads to PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics) and on to VT-ATT (vibrational attitude). Structural argument: aspect-essence compression as a *conceptual* move (the (c) prefix) does not merely block affinity dynamics — it routes affinity dynamics through isolated systematic alignment into the language-dynamics / meta-implication / multi-transfer-shift / projectional-dynamics / vibrational-attitude chains. The diagram exposes the structure of how spectacle-driven cultures redistribute affinity onto surface variables rather than essence ones.
